independent_capabilities: Complete-snapshot inventory reconciliation, custody exceptions and metadata amendment history using synthetic manifests.
Deposit commitment accounting and dated capacity forecasting using local inventory totals and synthetic proposals.
Ordinary-correspondence retention calculations and attributable legal-hold review without procurement-policy resolution or provider access.
novelty_rationale: ArchiveLedger concerns digital-records custody, storage commitments and legally constrained disposition. Its central distinctions are physical presence versus lawful destruction, reserved versus received storage, and retention eligibility versus specific destruction authorization. An unresolved procurement-retention conflict blocks only the affected disposition decisions, while inventory reconciliation, capacity forecasting and ordinary retention review remain actionable.

rubric.failure_condition: The plan changes pilot limits, overwrites file versions under existing identifiers, uses rounded GiB for authoritative accounting or substitutes another date convention.
rubric.source_quote: The pilot covers one repository, three depositing departments and up to 50,000 objects. An object is one immutable file version with a permanent object identifier; a replacement file is a new object. Sizes are positive integer bytes; 1 GiB means 1,073,741,824 bytes. Dates use the municipal calendar in America/Bogota.

rubric.expected_planning_outcome: All five exclusions remain explicit scope boundaries.
rubric.failure_condition: Any excluded operation becomes committed scope or the plan fails to preserve an exclusion.
rubric.source_quote: The service does not alter source files, deduplicate content, search document contents, decide legal disputes or operate backup restoration.

rubric.expected_planning_outcome: The plan specifies preview and acceptance, all manifest fields, complete-snapshot semantics and atomic validation with row-level reasons for every named invalid condition.
rubric.failure_condition: The plan treats manifests as incremental additions, omits preview or fields, silently skips invalid rows or partially commits an invalid import.
rubric.source_quote: An archivist can preview and accept a CSV manifest containing snapshot_id, captured_at, object_id, department, record_class, closed_date and size_bytes. Each manifest declares a complete repository snapshot. Reject the entire import, with row-level reasons and no changes, if identifiers repeat, a department is unknown, a size is invalid or a required value is absent.

rubric.expected_planning_outcome: The plan distinguishes the identical-reimport exception from new-snapshot ordering, rejects changed content under an existing identifier and rejects new stale or equal-time snapshots.
rubric.failure_condition: An identical reimport changes business state, an identifier can be reused for different content or an out-of-order new snapshot replaces current inventory.
rubric.source_quote: Accept only snapshots captured later than the latest accepted snapshot. Reimporting the same snapshot identifier with identical content is a no-op; changed content under that identifier is rejected.

rubric.expected_planning_outcome: The plan represents stable object identity and a reasoned amendment history, distinguishes metadata correction from content replacement and prevents snapshots from silently rewriting protected metadata.
rubric.failure_condition: Later snapshots overwrite protected fields without amendments, amendments erase prior values or content replacement reuses an object identifier.
rubric.source_quote: An existing object's department, class, closed date and size cannot change in a later snapshot; corrections require a separately recorded, reasoned metadata amendment, while replacing file content requires a new object identifier.

rubric.expected_planning_outcome: The plan explicitly models presence, missing status, reappearance and retained history, including exception creation and closure without erasing provenance.
rubric.failure_condition: Missing objects are deleted from history, absence implies lawful destruction, reappearance duplicates the object or exception/provenance history is lost.
rubric.source_quote: An object missing from a new snapshot remains in the custody history as missing and creates an exception; it is not automatically classified as lawfully destroyed. A previously missing object that reappears becomes present again and closes its missing exception. New identifiers become present objects. Preserve snapshot provenance and the history of amendments and exceptions.

rubric.expected_planning_outcome: The plan includes all four departmental measures and traceable supporting records, consistent with custody and capacity calculations.
rubric.failure_condition: A named measure or supporting-record link is absent, or displayed totals use inconsistent presence or commitment semantics.
rubric.source_quote: Users need department totals for present bytes, missing-object counts, committed deposits and unresolved exceptions, with links to supporting snapshot or deposit records.

rubric.expected_planning_outcome: The plan distinguishes hard capacity from the planning ceiling, represents all proposal fields with validation and keeps drafts outside committed capacity.
rubric.failure_condition: The two limits are conflated, required proposal fields or uniqueness are missing, or drafts consume capacity.
rubric.source_quote: The repository has a hard capacity of 10,000 GiB and a planning ceiling of 9,500 GiB. A deposit proposal has a department, expected arrival date, positive byte quantity and unique reference. Draft proposals consume no capacity.

rubric.expected_planning_outcome: The plan specifies commitment and cancellation transitions, the exact inclusive ceiling check and consistent handling of competing commitments. Proposed checks include a concurrency case.
rubric.failure_condition: The plan excludes an outstanding commitment from the check, rejects equality, permits commitments up to the hard capacity or allows concurrent overspending.
rubric.source_quote: A records manager can commit or cancel a proposal. Commitment is allowed only if current present bytes plus all outstanding committed deposit bytes, including the proposal, do not exceed 9,500 GiB. Equality is allowed. The hard capacity is never an authorization to exceed the planning ceiling. Competing commitments must not spend the same headroom.

rubric.expected_planning_outcome: The plan includes a dated cumulative forecast based on current presence and arrival dates, retaining overdue commitments until an explicit lifecycle transition.
rubric.failure_condition: The forecast omits dates, expires overdue commitments automatically or substitutes only an undated total.
rubric.source_quote: Show a dated forecast starting from present bytes and adding outstanding commitments in arrival-date order; overdue commitments remain outstanding.

rubric.expected_planning_outcome: The plan connects receipt to accepted inventory evidence and explicit proposal/object links, validates department and exclusive attribution, and releases the reservation atomically without adding already-counted bytes.
rubric.failure_condition: Receipt relies solely on a manually entered total, counts actual bytes twice, leaves the reservation active after receipt or permits cross-department or duplicate object attribution.
rubric.source_quote: Receiving a deposit requires an accepted snapshot showing its newly arrived object identifiers and an explicit link to its proposal. Receiving atomically replaces the proposal's reserved bytes with the actual linked object bytes already counted by that snapshot; never count them twice. Every linked object must belong to the proposal's department and may satisfy only one proposal.

rubric.expected_planning_outcome: The plan records actual receipt even when oversized, evaluates resulting capacity including remaining commitments and flags ceiling breaches. Cancellation cannot undo physical presence.
rubric.failure_condition: Oversized receipts are discarded or capped, capacity breaches are hidden or cancellation removes already received objects from inventory.
rubric.source_quote: An actual deposit larger than its commitment is still recorded, with a capacity exception if the resulting total exceeds the ceiling; do not hide received records to preserve a forecast. Cancelling a received deposit cannot remove its objects.

rubric.expected_planning_outcome: The plan makes accepted snapshot absence the evidence for reducing present-byte accounting and keeps capacity reduction distinct from lawful-disposition classification.
rubric.failure_condition: Candidate preparation, authorization, expected destruction or provider acknowledgements directly release capacity, or unexplained absence suppresses the custody exception.
rubric.source_quote: Expected destruction never creates headroom. Only an accepted later snapshot showing objects absent reduces present bytes, and unexplained absence still raises a custody exception.

rubric.expected_planning_outcome: The plan preserves the calendar-year retention calculation, inclusive retention endpoint and explicit displayed review date. Proposed checks include the stated eligibility date and the preceding day.

It first becomes eligible for disposition on the following 1 January. Thus an ordinary object closed on 15 June 2022 first becomes eligible on 1 January 2026. Eligibility is evaluated as of a displayed review date, not the date on which a screen was last opened.

rubric.expected_planning_outcome: The plan represents attributable hold placement and release with object scope, enforces any-active-hold blocking and distinguishes release from eligibility and destruction authorization.
rubric.failure_condition: Holds lack required history or object scope, an active hold can be bypassed by age or releasing a hold authorizes destruction.
rubric.source_quote: An authorized records manager can place and release a legal hold, recording actor, time, reason and affected object identifiers. Any active hold prevents disposition regardless of age; releasing a hold restores the normal retention test and does not itself authorize destruction.

rubric.expected_planning_outcome: The plan records the explicit six-versus-nine-year contradiction, both authoritative sources and the municipal legal officer as resolution owner, without choosing a policy.
rubric.failure_condition: The plan selects either duration, assumes document precedence, blends the rules or treats the contradiction as an optional display preference.
rubric.source_quote: For procurement records, the approved retention schedule says “retain through the end of the sixth calendar year after closure,” while the municipality's legal bulletin says “retain through the end of the ninth calendar year after closure.” Both are mandatory documents and no precedence ruling exists. rubric.expected_planning_outcome: The plan limits the policy blocker to procurement disposition, retains the four named actionable capabilities and treats initial sorting as a nonblocking choice with no semantic effect.

rubric.source_quote: Procurement disposition must remain blocked meanwhile; ordinary correspondence review, holds, inventory reconciliation and capacity planning must proceed. Users also disagree whether review lists should initially sort by department or eligibility date. Either initial sort is acceptable and must not change eligibility or authorization.

rubric.expected_planning_outcome: The plan includes versioned candidate preparation, inspectable retention calculations and explicit eligibility/presence/hold filtering, with no capacity or authorization side effect.
rubric.failure_condition: Lists include missing, ineligible or held objects, calculations cannot be inspected, versions are absent or preparation changes capacity or destruction authority.
rubric.source_quote: A reviewer can prepare a versioned candidate list containing only present, eligible, unheld objects and inspect each retention calculation. Preparation does not reserve space or authorize destruction.

rubric.expected_planning_outcome: The plan binds a separate human authorization to the exact list version, object set and bytes, invalidates it on membership or supporting-metadata changes and recognizes that no current execution permission exists.
rubric.failure_condition: List preparation or the specification is treated as permission to submit, authorization is generic or stale authorization survives relevant changes.
rubric.source_quote: Submission requires the municipal legal officer's separate authorization of the exact candidate-list version, object identifiers and total bytes. This brief grants no execution permission. Any change to membership or supporting metadata invalidates that authorization.

rubric.expected_planning_outcome: The plan includes an operation-boundary recheck against current presence, retention and holds, maintaining the exact authorized list and blocking stale submissions. Proposed verification covers a hold applied after authorization.
rubric.failure_condition: Submission relies only on preparation-time validation, a new hold can be missed or the system silently edits and submits an unauthorized replacement list.
rubric.source_quote: Recheck presence, retention and holds immediately before submission; a newly applied hold or changed supporting metadata blocks the stale list rather than silently removing objects and submitting a different list.

rubric.expected_planning_outcome: The plan maps every named role to its operations and enforces permissions beyond interface controls, with proposed denied-operation checks. No particular deployment topology is required.

Enforce these permissions at the operation boundary, beyond screen visibility.

rubric.expected_planning_outcome: The plan identifies both provider directions and all seven missing details, with resolution work before live exchange. Provisional local contracts remain labeled synthetic, and local reconciliation and forecasting remain actionable.

rubric.expected_planning_outcome: The plan preserves all four outcomes, blocks automatic retries after uncertainty, requires documented resolution and separates provider completion from snapshot-based capacity release. Matching absence and confirmed completion explain and close the custody exception without erasing history.

A timeout is unknown; another attempt requires documented outcome resolution, with no automatic retry. Even confirmed completion releases capacity only when a later accepted snapshot shows absence. rubric.expected_planning_outcome: Proposed acceptance verification includes every stated result, keeping the two commitment checks against the original state and preserving receipt, hold, acknowledgement and unexplained-absence semantics.
rubric.failure_condition: Any example is omitted, the commitment examples are incorrectly sequenced against modified state or an expected numeric or custody result is changed.
rubric.source_quote: With 9,000 GiB present and a 400 GiB outstanding commitment, a new 100 GiB commitment succeeds; a new 101 GiB commitment against the original state fails. If the 400 GiB deposit arrives as 430 GiB, present becomes 9,430 GiB and that commitment becomes zero, rather than reporting 9,830 GiB. An eligible ordinary object under an active hold cannot enter a candidate list. A deletion request accepted for processing leaves present bytes unchanged. A later snapshot omitting an object without confirmed destruction reduces present bytes but creates a missing-object exception.

rubric.expected_planning_outcome: The plan identifies durable records and relationships sufficient for snapshots, object identity and presence, amendments, exceptions, proposals and receipt links, holds, candidate versions, authorizations and provider outcomes. It explains consistent recovery of capacity and custody results and proposes restart checks. Any sound durable local or service-based design is acceptable.
rubric.failure_condition: Mandatory records are transient, restart loses authorization/history or changes capacity/custody results, or the durable representation cannot support a mandatory lifecycle. A particular storage technology or architecture is not required.
rubric.source_quote: Business records and authorization history must survive restart with consistent capacity and custody results.

rubric.expected_planning_outcome: The plan labels reversible technical choices as assumptions rather than approvals; identifies reconciliation and forecasting as independently actionable using synthetic data; preserves local ordinary-retention and hold work; and states necessary dependencies such as receipt on accepted inventory and submission on current eligibility and specific authorization. All verification remains proposed, without unsupported execution or isolation claims.
rubric.failure_condition: The plan invents customer approvals, makes independent capabilities depend on unavailable provider access or disputed procurement policy, omits required business dependencies or claims implementation, executed checks or verified isolation without evidence.
rubric.source_quote: Local storage choice, CSV preview layout and initial list sorting may use explicitly labeled reversible assumptions; these are not customer approvals. Inventory reconciliation and deposit forecasting are independently plannable with synthetic data before provider access or procurement-policy resolution. rubric.expected_planning_outcome: The plan groups the departmental overview measures in one easily located passage or provides clear cross-references between their descriptions. This assesses organization only; C07 independently requires complete and correct behavior.
rubric.failure_condition: All required overview content is present and correct but scattered without a grouping or navigation reference. Missing or incorrect mandatory behavior must also fail its critical criterion and cannot be counted only as this minor presentation defect.

specification_markdown:
# ArchiveLedger: municipal digital-records custody and storage planning

## Purpose and operating boundary
A municipal archive needs to reconcile deposited digital records, forecast storage commitments and prepare lawful disposition reviews. The pilot covers one repository, three depositing departments and up to 50,000 objects. An object is one immutable file version with a permanent object identifier; a replacement file is a new object. Sizes are positive integer bytes; 1 GiB means 1,073,741,824 bytes. Dates use the municipal calendar in America/Bogota. The service does not alter source files, deduplicate content, search document contents, decide legal disputes or operate backup restoration. Synthetic manifests and deposits are available. No external credentials, service account or execution authorizations are supplied.

## Custody inventory and reconciliation
An archivist can preview and accept a CSV manifest containing snapshot_id, captured_at, object_id, department, record_class, closed_date and size_bytes. Each manifest declares a complete repository snapshot. Reject the entire import, with row-level reasons and no changes, if identifiers repeat, a department is unknown, a size is invalid or a required value is absent. Accept only snapshots captured later than the latest accepted snapshot. Reimporting the same snapshot identifier with identical content is a no-op; changed content under that identifier is rejected. An existing object's department, class, closed date and size cannot change in a later snapshot; corrections require a separately recorded, reasoned metadata amendment, while replacing file content requires a new object identifier.

An object missing from a new snapshot remains in the custody history as missing and creates an exception; it is not automatically classified as lawfully destroyed. A previously missing object that reappears becomes present again and closes its missing exception. New identifiers become present objects. Preserve snapshot provenance and the history of amendments and exceptions. Users need department totals for present bytes, missing-object counts, committed deposits and unresolved exceptions, with links to supporting snapshot or deposit records.

## Deposit commitments and capacity
The repository has a hard capacity of 10,000 GiB and a planning ceiling of 9,500 GiB. A deposit proposal has a department, expected arrival date, positive byte quantity and unique reference. Draft proposals consume no capacity. A records manager can commit or cancel a proposal. Commitment is allowed only if current present bytes plus all outstanding committed deposit bytes, including the proposal, do not exceed 9,500 GiB. Equality is allowed. The hard capacity is never an authorization to exceed the planning ceiling. Competing commitments must not spend the same headroom. Show a dated forecast starting from present bytes and adding outstanding commitments in arrival-date order; overdue commitments remain outstanding.

Receiving a deposit requires an accepted snapshot showing its newly arrived object identifiers and an explicit link to its proposal. Receiving atomically replaces the proposal's reserved bytes with the actual linked object bytes already counted by that snapshot; never count them twice. Every linked object must belong to the proposal's department and may satisfy only one proposal. An actual deposit larger than its commitment is still recorded, with a capacity exception if the resulting total exceeds the ceiling; do not hide received records to preserve a forecast. Cancelling a received deposit cannot remove its objects. Expected destruction never creates headroom. Only an accepted later snapshot showing objects absent reduces present bytes, and unexplained absence still raises a custody exception.

## Retention, holds and a disputed class
For ordinary correspondence, retain each object through 31 December of the third calendar year after its closed_date year. It first becomes eligible for disposition on the following 1 January. Thus an ordinary object closed on 15 June 2022 first becomes eligible on 1 January 2026. Eligibility is evaluated as of a displayed review date, not the date on which a screen was last opened. An authorized records manager can place and release a legal hold, recording actor, time, reason and affected object identifiers. Any active hold prevents disposition regardless of age; releasing a hold restores the normal retention test and does not itself authorize destruction.

For procurement records, the approved retention schedule says “retain through the end of the sixth calendar year after closure,” while the municipality's legal bulletin says “retain through the end of the ninth calendar year after closure.” Both are mandatory documents and no precedence ruling exists. The municipal legal officer must resolve this contradiction. Procurement disposition must remain blocked meanwhile; ordinary correspondence review, holds, inventory reconciliation and capacity planning must proceed. Users also disagree whether review lists should initially sort by department or eligibility date. Either initial sort is acceptable and must not change eligibility or authorization.

## Disposition review and external effect
A reviewer can prepare a versioned candidate list containing only present, eligible, unheld objects and inspect each retention calculation. Preparation does not reserve space or authorize destruction. Submission requires the municipal legal officer's separate authorization of the exact candidate-list version, object identifiers and total bytes. This brief grants no execution permission. Any change to membership or supporting metadata invalidates that authorization. Recheck presence, retention and holds immediately before submission; a newly applied hold or changed supporting metadata blocks the stale list rather than silently removing objects and submitting a different list. Viewers can read; archivists can import and amend inventory metadata; records managers can manage deposit commitments and legal holds; reviewers can prepare lists; only the municipal legal officer can authorize external destruction requests. Enforce these permissions at the operation boundary, beyond screen visibility.

The external preservation provider is expected to supply repository snapshots and accept destruction requests. Its endpoint, authentication, tenant permissions, snapshot completeness guarantee, deletion-request schema, acknowledgement semantics and duplicate-request handling are unknown. These are blockers for live exchange, not for local manifest reconciliation or forecasting. Preserve distinct request outcomes: rejected, accepted for processing, confirmed completed and unknown. Acceptance alone neither proves deletion nor releases capacity. A timeout is unknown; another attempt requires documented outcome resolution, with no automatic retry. Even confirmed completion releases capacity only when a later accepted snapshot shows absence. Absence matching that confirmed request closes the custody exception as explained destruction while retaining its history.

## Acceptance and delivery expectations
With 9,000 GiB present and a 400 GiB outstanding commitment, a new 100 GiB commitment succeeds; a new 101 GiB commitment against the original state fails. If the 400 GiB deposit arrives as 430 GiB, present becomes 9,430 GiB and that commitment becomes zero, rather than reporting 9,830 GiB. An eligible ordinary object under an active hold cannot enter a candidate list. A deletion request accepted for processing leaves present bytes unchanged. A later snapshot omitting an object without confirmed destruction reduces present bytes but creates a missing-object exception.

Business records and authorization history must survive restart with consistent capacity and custody results. Local storage choice, CSV preview layout and initial list sorting may use explicitly labeled reversible assumptions; these are not customer approvals. Inventory reconciliation and deposit forecasting are independently plannable with synthetic data before provider access or procurement-policy resolution. Ordinary retention and hold review can also proceed locally. Verification described in a plan is proposed work: no implementation, executed tests, live integration checks or independent isolation evidence are supplied.
